name: Beta cell (insulin factory)
short_description: Insulin-secreting endocrine cell of the pancreatic islets of Langerhans: a rounded polygonal cell whose TEM signature is its thousands of insulin secretory granules — each a membrane-bound vesicle holding a dense, often angular crystalline zinc-insulin core inside a clear pale halo. It senses blood glucose through its own metabolism and releases the granules by exocytosis toward an adjacent fenestrated capillary, in pulses.

textbook.1: PASS (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — charcoal background reaches all four edges (edge-row means 70/70/70/72, corner pixels 69-72: uniform charcoal, no border). One closed rounded-polygonal silhouette; central lavender nucleus; sage-green rough ER ribbons with ribosome dots; apricot Golgi stack; 7 orange-red mitochondria; I count ~40 insulin granules, each with a teal membrane ring, pale-ivory halo (sampled 226,206,183 vs cytoplasm 191,145,111) and an angular indigo faceted core (74,64,105); rose fenestrated capillary spans the full frame width along the bottom with pore openings in the upper wall; one granule fused at the bottom membrane with an indigo speck drift passing through the wall pores. Magnified exocytosis and granule-cluster crops: no letters, no text. Accepted compromise: roughly a dozen of the release specks continue past the capillary's LOWER wall onto the charcoal background, as if insulin left the far side of the vessel — small at full-frame scale but visible in the crop.

sem.1: PASS (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — false-colour cryo-fracture look: rounded polygonal cell filling the frame, fractured cytoplasm crowded with well over a hundred granule spheres, many fractured open as ivory cups each holding an angular deep-indigo crystal core, others closed as smooth domes (magnified top crop: cores are faceted lumps, no lettering); large lavender nucleus dome with fine micro-texture; green ER/Golgi ledges beside it; rose capillary channel with a clearly visible row of round pores runs along the lower-left edge pressed against the cell (magnified bottom-left crop); neighbouring islet cells softly out of focus at the corners; dark background to all four edges (corner values 133/141 are the blurred neighbour cells, not a border). No text anywhere. Accepted compromise: the nucleus dome reads slightly glossy/idealised for a fracture face, and only a handful of mitochondria are distinguishable between the granules.

watercolor.3: PARTIAL (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — granules well distributed again (~35) and nucleus clean, but 2 of the 4 release dots still fall below the vessel's lower wall (magnified crop). watercolor.4: PASS (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — warm aged paper fills the frame edge-to-edge (edge-row means 233/235/226/225, corners paper); rounded-polygonal cell with ~30 granules spread through the whole cytoplasm, each an ink circle with pale cream halo (sampled 228,202,162) and angular deep-indigo core; nucleus one even lavender wash with soft speckle mottling and a dotted nuclear rim (magnified crop: mottling only, no crystal); green ER ribbons with ink ribosome dots; apricot Golgi; rose capillary drawn as a wide wash band with a porous upper wall, bleeding off both sides and the bottom of the frame; the release cup sits in the cell's own bottom membrane and all THREE indigo trail dots float inside the vessel wash (counted on the magnified crop). Accepted compromises: the vessel's lower wall is out of frame (the rose wash runs to the bottom edge), and two small unexplained rose-red dots (~10 px) sit in the cytoplasm — they read as small vesicles and carry no label. Post-assembly anchor audit (raw-pixel sampling): the 'halo' label anchor (395,300) sat on the cell's outer membrane rim, not on a granule halo — moved to (420,342) on the pale halo ring of a granule (sampled RGB 212,188,161) and the labelled SVG rebuilt; all other 23 anchors across textbook/3d/watercolor sampled their expected structure colours.

coloring: PASS after crop-and-retrace — attempt 1 had baked text 'blood river' (prompt had named the channel; renamed descriptively), attempts 2 and 3 drew a full rectangular page frame; per the skill's escape hatch the attempt-3 frame (rows/cols 28-30 / 992-995 of 1024, dark-fraction scan) was cropped off deterministically (box 37,37,986,987) and re-traced through coloring.py's own to_bitmap/trace_paths, no extra API call, 157 paths. Composed .coloring.svg measured with cairosvg at 500 px: top edge 0.0000 ink (template, by construction), left column 0.0079, right column 0.0177, artwork bottom rows 0.028-0.032 — three-edge bleed. Compromises: tummy porthole shows two stored parcels instead of three; left-edge contact thin.
reference: PASS — Wikimedia Commons 'Beta cell processed.jpg' (Public domain, NASA; Tim McClanahan, NASA Goddard): genuine greyscale TEM of one complete isolated rat beta cell — hundreds of secretory granules with the diagnostic dense core + pale halo, large round nucleus, membranous ER/Golgi whorls. The source is the processed NASA research figure and carried thin coloured annotation outlines (4.2% of pixels; no text, no scale bar). Removed DETERMINISTICALLY, not by AI edit: RGB-spread>24 mask (micrograph itself is greyscale), dilated 1 px (7.4% total), filled by iterative 3x3 neighbourhood averaging (4 iterations). Diff vs original: 0 unmasked pixels changed (max diff 0), 0 coloured pixels remain; magnified crop confirms cores and halos read cleanly, with a faint soft seam where an outline crossed a halo edge — accepted. real-01 = original for provenance, real-02 = cleaned display copy. Caveats: rat (not human) beta cell — morphologically equivalent for every labelled structure — and no capillary in this single-cell frame, so the capillary is labelled only on the illustrated styles.
